title: AgentCraft: Putting the Orc in Orchestration — Ido Salomon
talk_summary: AgentCraft is a game-inspired orchestration UI that visualizes live coding agents, file-level work, collisions, and human handoffs. Its practical ideas are review bundles with visual evidence, containerized campaign orchestration, agent-generated work, and shared human-agent awareness, but the talk cites no measured results.

takeaways.what_they_do: Bundles each PR-like change with task context, rationale, and screenshots/videos so the reviewer can inspect why the change happened and see visual proof.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can see exactly what changes happened in each one. Like why did they do stuff? What are the tasks? And I also have visual evidence.

takeaways.what_they_do: A broad goal is run in a container where agents decompose and plan it, while a campaign orchestrator handles babysitting and only escalates plan/review points.
takeaways.evidence_quote: once it's decomposed, I'm not the one doing the babysitting. Now, I have the campaign orchestrator and that's his problem.

takeaways.what_they_do: Maps the filesystem to visible rooms, tracks which agent is editing which file, and uses a heatmap to spot and proactively prevent collisions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can actually try and see visualize collisions and I can even prevent them proactively.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents are told to find missions/quests, and cron-style jobs can scan for ideas and implement them while the human decides what to keep.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I told them, "Okay, find missions for me to do." So, I have quests now

takeaways.what_they_do: Uses a fast cycle/queue for agents that need plan approval or answers to questions, modeled on RTS muscle memory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: quickly cycle between the agents that need our help. They need us to approve the plan. They need us to answer some questions

takeaways.what_they_do: Shared workspaces and chat let humans and agents see each other’s active work and files, so agents know when someone else is already working.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the next time the agent does something, it knows someone else is working. They can also have soft collaboration
